blocks.content: Constitutional bodies derive their power directly from the Constitution of India, making any structural modification subject to a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

items: Distinguish between Statutory Bodies (e.g., NHRC, SEBI) and Constitutional Bodies (e.g., CAG, UPSC) for prelims questions.
Remember that National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) gained constitutional status via the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 (Article 338B).
NITI Aayog is neither a statutory nor a constitutional body; it was established via an executive resolution.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional bodies derive their powers, duties, and existence directly from the Constitution of India.
Any amendment to the structure or powers of a constitutional body requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
Key examples include the Election Commission (Article 324), Comptroller and Auditor General (Article 148), and Finance Commission (Article 280).
Non-constitutional bodies are classified into statutory bodies (created by an Act of Parliament) and executive bodies (created by executive resolution).
